source.quote: A significant coastal urban area in the Mediterranean

clues.text: This city sits on the coast in south Europe, right by the sea. A high rocky hill stands at its heart.

clues.narrowing: Rules out cool-summer coasts; keeps hot cities that heat themselves.

source.quote: Athens may get particularly hot in the summer, owing partly to the strong urban heat island effect characterising the city.

clues.text: Summers turn fierce here, in part since the built up streets trap heat. The packed city makes its own hot air and holds it close.

clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to small old towns raised to capital of a new free state in 1834.

source.quote: Athens was chosen to replace Nafplio as the second capital of the newly independent Greek state in 1834, largely because of historical and sentimental reasons.

clues.text: In 1834 this small town was picked as the new capital of a free land. Leaders chose it for its grand past and deep meaning.

clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one famous stone temple on a central rock, from the age when free votes began.

clues.text: A grand stone temple crowns the steep rock at the heart of this town. It was built in a golden age when free votes first shaped the land.

clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the national parliament sits in this city, in a former royal palace.

source.quote: the new palace of the Bavarian king (now housing the Greek Parliament )

clues.text: The parliament of Greece makes its laws in this city. Its members meet in a grand old palace built for a king.

reveal.blurb: This town began more than 3,000 years ago and gave the world its first taste of rule by free votes. In 1834 it was picked as the capital of a free land, and a grand temple still crowns its rock. Today crowds climb to that temple and lawmakers meet in an old palace. Athens is the capital of Greece.
